solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lass declared so wicked in ancient documents

indicators.note: something wicked is twisted or bad, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl's announcement shows up as a nasty note in old manuscripts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' signals rearranging LASS DECLARED SO, all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrolls found near Qumran are among the oldest surviving biblical manuscripts.

clue.text: After party drink those people annoy someone who denies others pleasure

indicators.note: the drink is placed after the party in the build

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone drinking after a party irritates a killjoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from Aesop, describes a spoilsport who keeps from others what they cannot use themselves.

clue.text: Judge arrives having snatched quick meal

indicators.note: the first piece grabs and holds the second inside it

parts.note: arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: A judge turns up after grabbing a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone appointed to settle a dispute, a synonym for judge.

clue.text: Words he's apt to get wrong as elected representative

indicators.note: getting something wrong muddles it, so the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A representative is liable to mix up his words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get wrong' rearranges WORDS HES APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A union member elected by colleagues to represent them at a workplace.

clue.text: Some plans were on offer to find a way out

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lying inside them

explanation.surface: Part of a proposal on the table offers an escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run from 'plans were'; 'on offer to find' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution to a problem is a way out of it, a synonym in this sense.

clue.text: Carol sung badly — son out making loud noise

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters of the song are jumbled
the son is put out, so his letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A carol performed poorly makes a racket once the boy leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes S from CAROL SUNG, and 'badly' rearranges the remaining CAROLUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Clangour is a continuous loud clanging or din.

clue.text: Solemn person to cry in the East End

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End famously drop their aitches, so the leading letter goes

parts.note: to howl is to cry loudly

explanation.surface: A serious person is weeping in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: London's East End is home to Cockney speech, which drops the H sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are proverbially wise and grave, so a solemn-looking person can be called one.

clue.text: What you get at a noisy gig may be well-worn

parts.note: a gig is a live performance
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A loud concert may leave things looking battered.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'What you get at a noisy gig' as LIVE DIN, a loud performance; 'may be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A lived-in room or garment looks comfortably used, shabby from wear.

clue.text: This water swirling accounts for lost branch line

indicators.note: swirling water churns things round, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Turbulent seas explain why a railway spur disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges LOST BRANCH LINE; 'accounts for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bristol Channel is the estuary inlet between south Wales and south-west England.

clue.text: Apes a composer of anthems and madrigals

definitions.text: a composer of anthems and madrigals
definitions.meaning: Orlando ..., English Tudor-Jacobean composer of church music and madrigals

explanation.definitionFit: Both the primates and the surname of the English composer Orlando share this spelling.

clue.text: Gangster and sweetheart getting everywhere

parts.note: Al Capone is the crossword's stock gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster and his girlfriend turn up all over town.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spread all over is found in every place, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Inedible 25 and bread sent back

indicators.note: sending back turns the word round

parts.note: a tin is a loaf baked in a tin

explanation.surface: An uneatable item and a loaf get returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is EGG; a nit is the egg of a louse, hardly food. A tin is a British loaf baked in a rectangular tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit is the egg of a louse, an egg nobody would eat.

clue.text: Raymond slithers, says Spooner? Anyone would, making these trips!

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

explanation.surface: Raymond is skidding about, so anyone would enjoy a winter outing.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of RAY SLIDES gives SLAY RIDES, which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleigh rides are trips over snow, and slithering suits them.

clue.text: Rogue — troubled parson is about to phone one

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the other pieces
a troubled person is unsettled, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A worried vicar is about to ring someone about a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'parson' looks like the clergyman of the surface, but 'troubled' marks his letters for rearranging into RAPSON, which 'is about' then wraps around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapscallion is a mischievous rascal, a synonym for rogue.

clue.text: Husband, not totally passionate, to become less sympathetic

indicators.note: the word is not given in full, so its last letter is cut

explanation.surface: A husband who is lukewarm grows colder towards his partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not totally' cuts the final T from ARDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To harden is to grow tough and unfeeling, losing sympathy.

clue.text: Happen to meet tramp needing drink by front of Odeon

parts.note: a pint is a drink of beer

indicators.note: the front of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A vagrant wanting a beer outside a cinema runs into someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Odeon is a British cinema chain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump into someone is an idiom for meeting them by chance.

clue.text: Let biro flow — time to get stuck into that text

indicators.note: the piece is placed inside the anagram
letting the letters flow sends them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Writer's advice: let the pen run and take time over the words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flow' rearranges LET BIRO into LIBRETO, and T goes in. A biro is a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera or musical.

clue.text: Maiden with opportunity to fling old shoe

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: flinging the letter away drops it from the word

explanation.surface: A girl gets a chance to throw away an ancient shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fling' drops the second O from OCCASION.
explanation.definitionFit: A moccasin is a soft leather slip-on shoe.

clue.text: Talk over water in the Loire valley? One may well have wine!

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

explanation.surface: Chatting by the river in France, someone produces wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Many French wine estates are named Château something.
explanation.definitionFit: A French wine estate is called a château, and its vineyard produces wine.

clue.text: Short account in which African dictator appears to be bitter

indicators.note: the dictator goes inside the account

parts.note: acc is a shortening of account

explanation.surface: A brief report featuring a Ugandan despot is sour in tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic means sharp or sour in taste or remark, a synonym of bitter.

clue.text: Sir does puzzle in several papers

indicators.note: to puzzle is to confuse, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A knight sets a riddle across several newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of documents on one subject.

clue.text: 'Inadequate cast no good' (press)

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A review of a poor theatre company, quoted from the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a crowd, as is a press of people.

clue.text: An adherent about fifty who is terribly behind the times?

definitions.text: who is terribly behind the times?

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters are turned around into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old follower is hopelessly old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges AN ADHERENT; 'terribly' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a Neanderthal means they are primitive and old-fashioned.

clue.text: Spring in a European country, not at home

indicators.note: the home part is not present, so it is removed

explanation.surface: A water source in Iberia, while the owner is away.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring.

clue.text: Heating wire in iron, say

definitions.meaning: the coil in a kettle or heater
iron is a chemical example of the basic substances

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a heating coil and a basic chemical substance such as iron.

clue.text: Food? Say grace initially

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter

explanation.surface: Before eating, say grace.
explanation.definitionFit: Food here is a broad category and the answer is one example of it, a staple eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Belief Greek character's got in head

indicators.note: the Greek letter is put inside

parts.note: onion is slang for head, as in use your onion

explanation.surface: A belief from Greece has entered somebody's head.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief held about something.

clue.text: Gargle one nurse prepared for medical officer

indicators.note: a prepared mixture is made up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A nurse makes up a mouthwash for the chief doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surgeon General is a senior medical officer, the chief of a public health service.
